reason: I'll build the receiving parts first: the arrows show the branches carrying messages toward the cell body.
expectation: The branches will attach to the nerve-cell bodies, completing the receiving regions.

alternatives.reason: Fitting channels to the fibres also supports a goal, but I want to start with where messages are received.

effect: The branches are attached, and the new goal is to bring blood beside the receiving cells.
reaction: The result was straightforward and matched what I expected.
reason: I'll add the blood vessels because the picture shows them supplying oxygen and food to cells.
expectation: The vessels will sit beside the nerve cells and supply them, though I don't know what this will unlock.

alternatives.reason: The channels are another goal, but I want to finish supplying the receiving cells first.

effect: The receiving cells now have nearby blood vessels, while the long fibres still need to be added.
reaction: The picture makes the blood supply clear, though the step was predictable.
reason: I'll fit the channels first because the intro says they let charged particles cross the fibre membrane.
expectation: The gated channels will be fitted into the long fibres' membranes, preparing them to carry electrical changes.

alternatives.reason: I could attach the fibres now, but I'd rather prepare their channels first.

effect: The channels show how an electrical change travels along the fibre, and the remaining goal is to join the prepared parts.
reaction: The neighbouring channels opening in turn was a helpful detail; I didn't know the signal worked that way.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and it joins the supplied receiving cells to the prepared fibres.
expectation: The fibres will connect to the nerve cells beside the blood vessels, forming nervous tissue.

effect: Joining the prepared parts completed the nervous tissue and all chapter goals, showing the nerve cells alongside their blood supply.
reaction: It was satisfying to see the two projects come together, though the final combination was predictable.

mostWorthwhile.text: Fitting the ion channels was most worthwhile because the sequence showed how an electrical change travels along a fibre.

leastWorthwhile.text: Adding blood vessels was clear but predictable; it mostly confirmed that nerve cells need food and oxygen.

surprise.text: I was surprised that neighbouring channels open in turn rather than one ion travelling the whole length of the fibre.

arbitrary.text: None felt especially arbitrary: the pictures and goals gave each combination a purpose, although the menu supplied compatible pairings.

continue.text: I would continue to see how the nervous tissue connects to other body systems; the channel explanation made me curious.
